reading.text:
Unit: def:LevyStochCalc.Brownian.augFiltration (reading locked before any Lean is seen)

Paper notion. Section 2, lines 222-229: the filtered space satisfies the usual conditions, and (F_t) is
"the usual augmentation" of the filtration generated by W, N and F_0. The usual augmentation of a
filtration (G_t) under P: F_t = intersection over u > t of sigma(G_u, null sets), where the null sets
are the P-null sets (of the completion of the ambient sigma-algebra, or of F); equivalently the
smallest filtration containing G that is complete (F_0 contains all P-null sets) and right-continuous.
For a filtration generated by a Levy process (here (W,N)) together with an independent F_0, adding the
null sets already yields right-continuity (Blumenthal-type 0-1 law), so "augmentation by null sets"
and "usual augmentation" coincide in the paper's setting.

What a faithful Lean definition must be.
- Given a filtration G and the probability P: F_t = G_t joined with the sigma-algebra generated by the
  P-null sets (sets of P-measure zero), possibly followed by right-continuous regularisation
  (intersection over u > t). Either is acceptable for the paper's generated filtration, by the remark
  above, provided the propositions are about that filtration; on a general filtration only the version
  with right-continuity is the usual augmentation.
- Lean caveat: the ambient MeasurableSpace is fixed and need not be complete. If "null sets" means sets
  of outer measure zero not necessarily measurable in the ambient sigma-algebra, F_t may fail to be
  <= the ambient sigma-algebra, so it would not be a Mathlib Filtration on that space; a faithful Lean
  version must either use null sets that are measurable (P-null sets in the ambient sigma-algebra) or
  work on a complete space. Using only measurable null sets is the augmentation relative to F, which is
  what the standard definition gives when F is complete, and is harmless otherwise because the
  measures of all relevant events and the a.s. statements are unchanged.
- The augmentation must be by P-null sets for THE probability measure of the paper (not e.g. an
  arbitrary measure), and must contain G_t.

comparison.text:
Comparison: def:LevyStochCalc.Brownian.augFiltration
(Brownian/AugmentedFiltration.lean:51-57; Probability/Augmentation.lean:45 for aug; uses in the
PaperSpec via Dissertation/WellPosedness/Enlarged/Filtration.lean: enlJoint = augFiltration
(initJoint).rightCont P.)

- Reading: the usual augmentation of G under P: null sets added (and right-continuity), the null sets
  being measurable ones so the result is <= the ambient sigma-algebra; adding null sets alone suffices for
  the paper's generated filtration; on a general filtration only the right-continuous version is the
  usual augmentation; augmentation by THE probability measure; contains G_t.
- Lean: augFiltration F mu at time t = aug (F (max t 0)) m_Omega mu, where aug m m0 mu = the m0-measurable
  sets A with mu(A sym-diff B) = 0 for some m-measurable B (= m joined with the m0-measurable mu-null
  sets, aug_eq_sup_nullSigma). So: null-set augmentation with ambient-measurable null sets (the Lean
  caveat of the reading is handled: <= ambient by aug_le), containing F_t (le_augFiltration), with the
  filtration frozen at its time-0 value for t < 0.
- Right-continuity: not part of this definition. It is the augmentation by null sets only. In the
  PaperSpec the standing filtration is enlJoint = augFiltration ((F^{W,N} v G_0)).rightCont P, the null-set
  augmentation of the right-continuous version, which is right-continuous (instance
  isRightContinuous_augFiltration, using that augmentation commutes with countable decreasing
  intersections) and complete at time 0: the usual augmentation. So the paper's notion is obtained by
  composing this definition with rightCont, as the reading anticipated.
- Measure: mu is a parameter; the PaperSpec passes the probability measure P.
- Freezing before 0: F_t := aug F_0 for t < 0; the paper has no negative times; it only makes the
  negative-time sigma-algebras larger, which affects no statement about [0,T].

Verdict: faithful with representation choices.

verdict.detail:
Representation choices, each harmless:
1. This definition is the augmentation by null sets only (no right-continuous regularisation). The paper's
   "usual augmentation" is obtained in the PaperSpec as augFiltration (G.rightCont) P (enlJoint), which is
   right-continuous and complete, i.e. the usual augmentation; and for the filtration generated by the
   Levy noise and an independent F_0 the null-set augmentation is already right-continuous, so in the
   paper's setting the two notions agree anyway.
2. The null sets are the mu-null sets measurable for the ambient sigma-algebra (aug relative to m_Omega),
   so the result is a Mathlib filtration on the given space; this is the standard augmentation when the
   space is complete, and on an incomplete space it changes no probability or almost-sure statement.
3. For t < 0 the filtration is frozen at aug F_0; the paper has no negative times, and the larger
   negative-time sigma-algebras affect no statement about [0,T].
4. The measure is a parameter; the PaperSpec instantiates it with the probability measure P.
